Q: In single-thread Rust, what's the most idiomatic or concise way to mut borrow one field in a struct and leave the rest available? A:

You should split Root into components. As small as possible. And then systems simply accept components they need. You then group components into entities. And now you've rediscovered the ECS pattern, so you may as well just use one of the existing ECS Rust libs. Which simplify and optimize the management and storage. That pattern was pretty much designed to be used in games. Where there are lots of entities, lots of components, lots of possible combinations of components and things change very dynamically.

Q: How do I setup pyspark in VS Code? A:

I had the same problem. It was solved by adding the following lines to <sparkHome>/conf/spark-env.sh:

export PYSPARK_PYTHON=python3.8
export PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON=python3.8

AND in vscode setting python interpreter to 3.8 too (you can set it from command palette and typing Python:Select Interpreter.

If you don't have spark-env.sh, make a copy of the template file already in the conf folder.

Q: Convert Integer to Date in Snowflake using Error Handling A:

I suggest you contact Snowflake support and ask them to enable try_to_date with format string - it's available but needs to be enabled manually.

However you have to be aware that TRY_TO_DATE on '20200034' will be resolved to NULL.
